body: A judge on the 19th Judicial District Court signed a temporary restraining order on Monday, July 13, 2026, barring the City of St. George from adopting or enforcing a proposed ordinance that would rezone a nearly 60-acre parcel near the Pecue Lane interchange with Interstate 10, The Advocate reported. The parcel is part of the Kleinpeter family's land. The city council had scheduled a public hearing and final action on the rezoning for the next day; instead, it voted to defer the item indefinitely because of the litigation. The article did not name the judge.

Landowner LRK LLC filed the suit on June 8. According to The Advocate, the suit says the land carried a heavy commercial classification from the East Baton Rouge Metro Council for more than three decades. On April 28, St. George approved a zoning overhaul that consolidated 45 districts into 16 and converted the C-2 classification into a mixed-use category. The parcel was reassigned to Mixed-Use Community 3 (MX-3), though the council had not voted on that change. LRK calls the change a "downzoning" that would limit the size and density of development and asks a judge to declare any more restrictive zoning for the tract unconstitutional and unenforceable.

WBRZ, citing the Baton Rouge Business Report, reported that the suit also asks the court to declare that St. George was never lawfully incorporated, arguing that no court ever entered an order formally declaring the city's incorporation date. Two leaders of the incorporation effort are also named as defendants. Mayor Dustin Yates said the city disagrees with the claims and will address them in court, adding that the Louisiana Supreme Court "ruled in favor of incorporation." After the restraining order, a city spokesperson said the city's position had not changed.
The order was to remain in place at least until a July 28 hearing on LRK's request for a preliminary injunction. The sources reviewed do not report the outcome of that hearing.

timeline.label: St. George approves a zoning-code overhaul consolidating 45 districts into 16
LRK LLC sues over the proposed rezoning of its tract and asks the court to declare St. George was never legally incorporated
19th Judicial District Court judge signs a TRO blocking the proposed rezoning
City council defers the rezoning indefinitely because of the litigation
